Troubleshooting

The most common problems across SATOM — sign-in, forms, permissions, appliances, jobs, scheduling, alerts, metrics, updates, HA and start-up — each with likely causes, a fix and how to confirm it, plus links to the detailed article.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
📍 WhereApplies to the whole application; server-side checks use the satom command on the node

Start here#

Most server-side problems are diagnosed with two commands on the node (any user):

satom get system health      # units, /healthz, disk — one roll-up
satom diagnose all           # every check, one exit code

A page that failed with Something went wrong shows an Error reference; an administrator finds the full failure with grep <reference> /opt/satom/data/logs/satom.log. Message texts are listed in Error messages; status values in Statuses.

Sign-in and session#

"Invalid username or password." although the password is right#

Possible causes - The account is local and the password differs from the directory one (local accounts never fall back to the directory). - A directory account was imported but not approved, or is disabled. - The node is reached over plain http:// (see the next problem).

Solution 1. Try another known-good account. 2. For directory users, test the source in Settings → Authentication. 3. An administrator can reset a password on the node: sudo satom execute admin reset-password <username> (audited as user cli/root). 4. Check the audit log: every failed local sign-in is recorded as login.fail, a failed directory sign-in as login.external_fail.

Verification — sign-in succeeds and the audit log shows a login entry.

Every password is refused and the page says the site is served over HTTP#

Possible causes - The browser reached SATOM over http://. The session cookie is marked Secure, so the browser never returns it and no sign-in can succeed.

Solution 1. Use https://satom.example.com/. 2. If HTTPS is broken, restore the TLS proxy (deploy/tls-bootstrap.sh), see Installation.

Verification — the sign-in form accepts the password over https://.

"Too many failed attempts — account temporarily locked. Try again later."#

Possible causes — 10 consecutive failed sign-ins on that account.

Solution — wait 15 minutes, or on the node: sudo satom execute admin unlock <username> (the password is unchanged).

Verification — the next correct sign-in works.

Every form says the session expired#

The message is "Your session expired or the form was stale — please try again.", on every POST including sign-in.

Possible causes - The reverse proxy sends proxy_set_header Host $host; and SATOM is reached on a non-standard port (or through NAT). $host drops the port, so the CSRF check compares the browser's Referer (with port) against a host without it and rejects every form. - A genuinely old form (the CSRF token lives one hour) — then it happens once, not every time.

Solution 1. In the proxy configuration use proxy_set_header Host $http_host;. 2. On a node whose vhost the installer wrote: sudo satom execute repair nginx --yes. 3. Reload nginx: sudo satom execute reload nginx.

Verification — satom diagnose nginx shows $http_host for every proxied vhost, and saving a form works. See Security model.

"Your session was locked after N minutes of inactivity."#

Possible causes — the browser session was idle for longer than Settings → General → Session Lock (minutes). Background refreshes (notification bell, job dock, status badges) do not count as activity, so a tab left open still locks.

Solution — sign in again; you return to the page you asked for. An administrator can change the timeout (5 to 1440 minutes, default 60).

Verification — the audit log shows session.idle_lock for the sign-out.

Rate limit on the sign-in page (429)#

Possible causes — more than 5 sign-in attempts per minute from one address. Behind an extra proxy that is not listed in TRUSTED_PROXIES, all users share the proxy's address and therefore one limit.

Solution — wait a minute; add the proxy address to TRUSTED_PROXIES in /opt/satom/.env and restart satom.service. See Configuration files.

Verification — the audit log shows real client addresses, not the proxy's.

Permissions and pages#

"Access denied" (403)#

Possible causes - Your profile lacks the permission the page or button needs. Every page that shows device content needs a read permission too: the Audit Log needs View audit log (audit.view); appliance list, detail and datasheet pages need View appliances (appliances.view); the FortiWeb workspace, protection, exceptions, artifacts, server objects, object editor, wizard and fleet objects need View protection (protection.view); Device Provisioning needs View operations (operations.view); the API-Registry Explorer and the FortiADC / FortiAnalyzer / FortiAuthenticator API consoles need View registry (registry.view); Sentinel needs View monitoring (monitoring.view); the DNS tool needs View network (network.view); the monitoring pages, attack search, the FortiADC / FortiAnalyzer / FortiAuthenticator pages, the transaction tracer and the certificate inspector need a view permission. Firmware upgrade, boot-partition switch and HA failover need Run appliance actions (appliances.apply). - You opened a bookmark or a shared link: the sidebar only shows the pages your profile can open, so a missing menu entry means the same thing as this 403. - Your address is not in the IP allow-list (administrators are exempt).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: pages that used to open for any signed-in user (Audit Log, monitoring, appliances, FortiWeb workspace and protection pages, FortiADC / FortiAnalyzer / FortiAuthenticator pages, Device Provisioning, API Explorer and product API consoles, Sentinel, DNS tool) now answer 403 without the matching read permission, and the sidebar hides links the user cannot open. Seeded profiles hold all read keys and are unaffected.

Solution — ask an administrator to check your profile in Users and profiles and the allow-list in Settings → Access Control. Every 403 is logged on the server as FORBIDDEN user=… ip=….

Verification — the page opens.

A page sends me to another place or to a different ADOM#

Possible causes - Pages belong to an ADOM (FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator, Global). Opening a page that does not exist in the current ADOM redirects to that ADOM's home. - FortiWeb device pages need a selected appliance; without one you land on the Architecture view.

Solution — switch ADOM with the ADOM picker or select an appliance first. See ADOMs and products.

Every page answers 503 for non-administrators#

Possible causes — the IP allow-list setting cannot be read (for example a damaged value after a restore). SATOM refuses rather than admit everyone.

Solution — an administrator (not affected) opens Settings → Access Control and saves a valid list.

Verification — non-administrators can open pages again.

Appliances#

A new appliance never syncs and stays unknown or offline#

Possible causes - Verify SSL Certificate is on for an appliance with a self-signed certificate: the TLS check fails before authentication. - Wrong host, port or credentials; the appliance's admin account is locked. - Network path from the node to the appliance is blocked.

Solution 1. Add the appliance's CA to the Trust store (preferred), or turn off Verify SSL Certificate on the appliance. 2. Check credentials and reachability on the appliance page (Appliances).

Verification — the status badge turns online and a sync completes.

A red banner "device error -20010 … license not valid"#

Possible causes — the appliance's licence is expired or flapping.

Solution — fix the licence on the appliance, then refresh. Pages keep working from the cache meanwhile.

"This object is locked by another user."#

Possible causes — another editor holds the edit lease.

Solution — wait: an abandoned lease expires after about two minutes, or take over the lock explicitly. See Locks.

Jobs and scheduling#

A job stays "running" after a restart#

Possible causes — the service restarted while the job's worker thread was running.

Solution — nothing: at start-up and then at most every two minutes SATOM marks such jobs error with "Orphaned — the service restarted while this job was running." Check the appliance and run the action again. To clean old entries: sudo satom execute repair jobs --yes.

Verification — the Job Manager no longer lists it as active.

Scheduled actions never fire#

Possible causes - No scheduled actions exist: the node has no appliance yet (the default set is created with the first one), or the rows were deleted. - This node is a standby: the scheduler only fires on the primary. - satom-scheduler.service is stopped, or cannot reach the database. - The action is disabled, or all its targets are in maintenance (skipped).

Solution 1. satom diagnose scheduler. 2. Create the recommended set: sudo satom execute seed actions --yes. 3. sudo satom execute restart scheduler.

Verification — satom get scheduler status shows recent runs. See Scheduled actions and Services and timers.

An action's last status is "missed"#

Possible causes — the scheduler was not running at the due time (or found the action overdue) and catch-up is off, so the run was skipped and the action was moved to its next run. The yellow missed badge explains this on hover.

Solution — check that satom-scheduler.service runs on the primary, and enable catch-up on the action if a late run is better than none, or run it manually.

Alerts and monitoring#

A device is red but no e-mail arrived#

Possible causes - The appliance is in maintenance (alerts suppressed by design). - Alerts are disabled or no recipient is set; SMTP delivery fails. - This node is the standby (notifications are primary-only).

Solution — check Settings → Email & Alerts and use Preview now (no send); run sudo satom execute alerts run --dry-run. A run that found alerts but reached nobody leaves satom-alerts.service in failed. If satom get alerts status shows last email: REFUSED, the alerts are being found and the mail transport is turning them away — fix the relay or switch the transport to an SMTP provider. If it shows deliverability: ERROR, the mail was delivered unsigned and is probably in the recipient's spam folder.

Verification — satom get alerts status. See Alerting.

Metrics panels show a query error or stay empty#

Possible causes - satom-metrics.service is not installed or not running (the binary was not available at install time). - Nothing collects: the metrics_scrape scheduled action does not exist.

Solution 1. sudo satom execute reinstall metrics-store. 2. sudo satom execute seed actions --yes (includes the 3-minute metrics scrape).

Verification — satom diagnose all reports the store as live; panels draw data after a few minutes. See Metrics.

Updates#

Update queued but nothing happens#

Possible causes — satom-updater.path is disabled on this node, so requests stay queued.

Solution — sudo satom execute enable updater (on both nodes).

Verification — satom get update history shows the runner picked it up.

An offline package is refused#

Possible causes — the preflight blocks it: untrusted signing key, wrong Python, missing wheels, too little disk, or a version below the package's minimum.

Solution — read the named checks on the Software Update page; install the release key with sudo satom execute trust add-key <key>.pub. See Offline updates.

"Blocked by the staged-rollout safeguard…"#

Possible causes — in a pair, the primary may only take a revision the standby has already validated.

Solution — update the standby first, wait for its health check, then the primary. See Software update.

The update shows "root-side refresh held"#

Possible causes — the node has a signed-release trust anchor, and deploy/ changed since the last signed release. The application was updated; the unit files, install scripts, operator CLI and runner copies were not.

Solution — on the primary, run sudo satom execute sign-release (a dry run that shows the deploy/ diff), then sudo satom execute sign-release --yes, and update again, standby first.

Verification — sudo satom get release trust shows that HEAD's deploy/ matches the newest signed commit. See Signed releases.

High availability#

Settings will not save on the second node#

Possible causes — that node is the standby; its database is a read-only replica.

Solution — make the change on the primary; it replicates. Files in data/ reach the standby within 5 minutes.

Verification — satom get node status shows which node is primary. See High availability.

The standby's replication lag keeps growing#

Possible causes — replication is not keeping up or is stalled.

Solution — read the replication card on the High Availability page. Do not promote a lagging standby; promotion is for a primary that is confirmed down.

Peer views show "not authenticated"#

Possible causes — the two nodes' clocks differ by more than 120 seconds, so each refuses the other's request signatures; or one node is not yet updated to the release that signs peer requests (expect about a minute of this while the standby catches up during an update).

Solution — synchronise both clocks with NTP, and finish the update on both nodes.

Verification — the peer's card on the High Availability page shows its role, revision and up again. See High availability.

Start-up and data#

The service does not start after editing .env#

Possible causes - SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI missing with FLASK_ENV=production. - FERNET_KEY missing.

Solution — restore the values; satom diagnose config checks the file. Restart with sudo satom execute restart web.

Verification — curl -k https://satom.example.com/healthz returns 200.

Stored appliance passwords no longer work after a rebuild#

Possible causes — the database was restored on a node with a different FERNET_KEY. Backup bundles never contain the key.

Solution — restore the original key from the sealed envelope (sudo satom execute unseal recovery) or from your exported copy, put it in .env, restart. If the key is lost, re-enter every appliance password.

Verification — satom diagnose recovery; appliances sync again. See Security model.

The disk is full#

Possible causes — growth of data/, the metrics store or bundles; a full disk stops PostgreSQL while /healthz may still answer 200.

Solution — satom get system disk shows what grows; sudo satom execute repair tmp --yes removes aged scratch files; configure the backup server so verified bundles leave the node.

Verification — free space above max(15 % of the volume, 3 GB).
